name: Vascular Lesion (Cherry Angioma / Hemangioma)
description: A vascular skin lesion is a collection of small blood vessels near the skin surface. The most common type is a cherry angioma, which looks like a bright red, smooth, small dome on the skin. They are non-cancerous and very common.
common_symptoms: Bright red, purple, or deep crimson dome-shaped spot
Smooth surface, usually 1 to 5 millimeters across
Can bleed briskly if scratched, cut, or rubbed
Most often found on the torso, arms, shoulders, or legs
causes: Benign proliferation and widening of superficial blood vessels (capillaries)
Exact cause is not fully known; strongly associated with natural aging and genetic factors
risk_factors: Age over 30 years (they increase in number with advancing age)
first_aid: If the spot is cut or bleeds, apply firm pressure with a clean cloth or gauze for 10 to 15 minutes
Keep the area elevated if on an arm or leg until bleeding stops
Apply a sterile adhesive bandage once bleeding is controlled
precautions: Avoid scratching, scrubbing, or shaving roughly over raised red spots
Protect skin from mechanical trauma or snagging on tight jewelry
Seek medical attention if bleeding does not stop after 20 minutes of firm pressure
home_care: Keep the spot clean with mild soap and water
Cover with a small plaster if it catches on clothing
do_not: DO NOT prick, scratch, or try to pop the red bump with a needle or pin
DO NOT apply burning chemicals or home remedies to remove blood spots
DO NOT pull away gauze abruptly while blood is clotting
red_flags: Continuous, rapid bleeding that will not stop after 20 minutes of steady pressure
A rapid-growing bleeding red lump that forms a collarette (may be a pyogenic granuloma)
A dark reddish-purple spot that develops jagged borders or turns black
when_to_see_doctor: See a healthcare provider if a red spot bleeds repeatedly, will not stop bleeding, grows very quickly, or changes to a dark uneven color.
prevention: There is no proven prevention as vascular spots are primarily linked to genetics and age
Protect skin from harsh abrasions and trauma

sources.title: Vascular Birthmarks and Lesions - American Academy of Dermatology
